nodes.text: Building and evaluating AI agents that act through software is engineering-heavy: interface, environment, interaction mechanism, benchmarks.
Software is a powerful interface to the world, so agents that write code, run commands and browse can act in complex ways; the authors also flag safety and side effects.
Existing frameworks: building blocks with basic runtime (LangChain), stateless execution (AutoGen), limited sandbox (CrewAI), SWE-specific agents.
No single framework, as the authors describe them, combines sandboxed execution, browser, reusable tools, delegation, a hub and evaluation for general agents.
RQ1: Can one open platform supply the shared abstraction, runtime, tools, delegation and evaluation needed to develop and evaluate agents?
RQ2: Is a single generalist agent on this platform competitive across software, web and assistance benchmarks?
Provide a community platform for generalist and specialist agents that interact with the world through software.
Event stream + docker runtime (bash, IPython, browser) + AgentSkills + delegation + evaluation harness, with a hub of community agents.
Architecture design: agent as function from event history to action, runtime as function from action to observation, sandbox per session.
The implemented system: three primitive actions, arbitrary docker images, skill library, delegation, hub, GUI, integration tests.
Evaluation protocol: 15 integrated benchmarks in three categories, evaluated 0-shot without benchmark-specific prompt engineering against open-source reproducible baselines.
Software engineering: SWE-Bench Lite 26.0% (claude-3-5-sonnet), 22.0% (gpt-4o), 7.0% (gpt-4o-mini); HumanEvalFix 79.3%.
Web browsing: WebArena 8.5/14.8/15.5% (BrowsingAgent); MiniWoB++ 27.2% and 40.8%.
Miscellaneous assistance: GAIA L1 30.2/32.1%; GPQA diamond 52.0%; AgentBench OS 57.6%; MINT math 77.3%, code 50.0%; ProofWriter 78.8%; EDA 38.0%.
OpenHands agents sit below at least one listed comparator on eight benchmarks (negative result).
Authors: the same CodeAct agent, unmodified, is competitive across three task categories; the tables are consistent with this but rest on single values and heterogeneous comparators.
The implemented components realise each of the five features the authors list; this is a description of the system rather than a measured property.
An open platform (five components plus 15-benchmark harness) with reference agents and reported evaluation results.
Single values, no spread; comparisons uncontrolled.
No empirical safety evaluation of sandbox and side effects.
Authors: agents struggle with complex tasks and long-file editing; workflow handcrafted.
The authors expect the platform to catalyse research and applications; untested beyond adoption statistics.
Multi-modality, browsing improvements (Auto Eval & Refine), stronger agents, better long-file editing, automatic workflow generation; later repositories (SDK, Agent Canvas).
Concepts: LLM agent, sandbox, IPython, SWE-Bench and resolve rate, hint text, CodeAct.

experiment_chains.experiment: Software engineering benchmarks (SWE-Bench Lite, HumanEvalFix; setup for BIRD, BioCoder, ML-Bench, Gorilla APIBench, ToolQA)
experiment_chains.hypothesis: A generalist CodeAct agent with a general action space is competitive with software-engineering specialists.
experiment_chains.falsifier: Scores far below open-source specialists on the same benchmark
experiment_chains.design_rationale: SWE-Bench Lite is the authors' default (cost saving); 0-shot without benchmark-specific prompts to test generality
experiment_chains.next: Does the same platform also support web browsing, a different action space?

experiment_chains.hypothesis: The browser action set plus delegation gives competitive results among agents using domain-general prompting.
experiment_chains.falsifier: Delegation from the generalist loses much relative to the dedicated browsing agent
experiment_chains.design_rationale: WebArena is realistic and hard; MiniWoB++ is synthetic and easier; both report the full set
experiment_chains.next: Do miscellaneous tool-use and reasoning tasks also run on the platform?

experiment_chains.experiment: Miscellaneous assistance benchmarks (GAIA, GPQA, AgentBench, MINT, ProofWriter, Entity Deduction Arena)
experiment_chains.hypothesis: The platform's tools and browsing support broad assistance tasks with one agent design.
experiment_chains.design_rationale: Covers tool use, multi-modality, OS interaction, multi-turn feedback, logic and state tracking
experiment_chains.next: What do the results establish and not establish, taken together?
